approach: Add `crates/athena-core/src/gate_counts.rs`, a pure function over `store::Records`. A gate is a failed check name in the verification of a `rejected` job, or `verifier` when none failed, or an admission violation rule on a rejected or failed job. A gate "ended" a job once per job. It was "overruled" when a later request job whose text is "try again on <job>" (found with `reading::retried_job`) landed the same change. "Same change" no longer compares whole-tree fingerprints alone, because they depend on the base. The rule: if both candidates carry `base_fingerprint` and the two are equal, the candidate `fingerprint`s must be equal. In every other case (bases differ, or either lacks a base fingerprint) the sorted `changes` lists (path, status, mode, bytes) must be equal and non-empty. The counts go three places. (1) The introspection prompt gets a `gate_counts` array, the schema enum gains `relax` and `remove`, and the system prompt says a rule or check can be wrong. (2) `PreventionKind` gains `Relax` and `Remove` (kebab-case serde; old kinds stay byte-identical). For these kinds the answer must carry a new nullable schema field `gate`, which must match a gate that has counts. Code stores it as a `[gate: NAME] ` prefix on `prevention`, anchored at the start of the text and read only for Relax and Remove. The docs call the prefix a stopgap until a typed field exists. (3) Hestia's `error_review` gets a branch for relax and remove that queues one normal-priority request, built with `StewardRequest`, naming the gate and citing its end and overruled counts and the introspection id. `cause_key` returns None for Relax and Remove, so they never join root-cause groups, and the gate request cannot suppress a root-cause request for other introspections. `athena status` gains a `gate_counts` field and a section, most overruled first. Nothing is relaxed or removed, and no config or workflow file is touched.

decisions.choice: Count from existing job records only (request, candidate, verification, outcome). 'Unchanged' is defined independently of the base: with equal Some base_fingerprints, the candidate fingerprints must be equal; otherwise the sorted non-empty `changes` lists (path, status, mode, bytes) must be equal. At most one end and one disagreement per gate per ended job, so disagreements <= ends.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The candidate fingerprint is a hash of the whole governed tree of the candidate commit (attrs.rs:135-160, candidate.rs:170-171), so any job landing on main between the rejected try and its retry changes it even for a byte-identical producer change. `ChangeEntry` (records.rs:718-723) and `Candidate.base_fingerprint` (records.rs:779) are in the records, so the base-independent comparison needs no new source. The retry link is `reading::retried_job`. A 'rejected' outcome is exactly a failed verification verdict (run/verification.rs:434-437), so the failed check names identify the gate.

rejected.why: Almost always differs once other jobs land between the two tries, so disagreements stay 0 in a busy repository and criterion 8 fails in real use.

rejected.option: Compare change lists only, never fingerprints
rejected.why: ChangeEntry holds byte counts but no content hash, so it is weaker evidence. When the base is identical the fingerprint is exact, so it is used there and the change list only when the base moved.

rejected.option: A new record kind or counter file for gate events
rejected.why: The brief rules out backfill and new sources; the records already hold every fact needed.

rejected.option: Also count a later green rerun or a verifier pass as disagreement
rejected.why: It needs a second, fuzzier signal and more fixtures. Criterion 1 only requires the unchanged-landing signal. Recorded as a user question.

decisions.choice: Name the gate through a new nullable answer field `gate` (`#[serde(default)]` in `Answer`). `apply_answer` checks it against the known gate names and stores `[gate: NAME] <prevention>` in the existing `prevention` field. `gate_of_prevention` anchors at the start of the text, requires the closing `] `, and Hestia calls it only when the kind is Relax or Remove. defaults-loop.md says the prefix is a stopgap until a typed field is added.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3 (accepted trade-off). `IntrospectionRecord` has `deny_unknown_fields`; a typed optional field would need edits at about 13 struct-literal sites outside the deliverables (refusal_corpus.rs:703, proposals.rs:742, evidence_labels.rs:521, labeled.rs:958, briefs.rs:3015, status.rs:2489/3462, hestia.rs:2856, introspect.rs:1355/1823, the CLI tests) and would change the record shape the brief puts out of scope. Readers that print `prevention` (retry_cause reading.rs:1482, mistake_report status.rs:1714, display.rs:1398/1463) show the marker as text, which names the gate and is harmless.

rejected.why: Out of scope ('changing existing introspection records') and forces edits in many unlisted files.

rejected.option: Find gate names inside the free `prevention` text
rejected.why: Names like `test` occur in any sentence, so the match would be wrong.

decisions.choice: Hestia queues the gate request for a single relax or remove introspection, without waiting for a repeated cause. The branch sits in `error_review` before `try_error_review`. It skips when `addressing_request` already finds a request citing that introspection id. `cause_key` returns None for Relax and Remove, so they never join a repeated-cause group.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. Criterion 2 needs one accepted answer to queue a request; the counts are the evidence. `addressing_request` (hestia.rs:282-324) treats a group as addressed when any request text contains any id in the group, so a gate-review request for a relax introspection B would hide a code-check A of the same cause from the backfill. Excluding Relax and Remove in `cause_key` (hestia.rs:264-274; only callers are hestia.rs:349 and :2372) keeps the gate request scoped to its own introspection, and a gate review does not claim to fix a root cause. The id citation is still used for the one-request-per-introspection idempotence check.

rejected.why: That path needs two or more distinct jobs with one cause, and its text asks for a root-cause fix, not a gate review.

rejected.option: Let relax and remove stay in cause groups and rely on the id citation to avoid a duplicate
rejected.why: The gate request would then suppress the root-cause request for the other introspections in the group (finding 2).

decisions.choice: Show gates in `athena status` as a `Vec<GateCount>` field skipped when empty, sorted by disagreements descending, then ends descending, then name.
decisions.reason: Existing status output and JSON stay unchanged when there are no gate ends. A reviewer reads the most overruled gate first (criterion 8). The label states the rule: 'overruled = a later try landed the same change'.

rejected.why: It would change every existing status output, and tests that match on text could break.

decisions.choice: Show criterion 6 by running fmt, clippy with -D warnings, and full-workspace test on the final tree.
decisions.reason: Adding enum variants and an `Answer` field can break compilation or lints in crates that were not edited; only a whole-workspace run proves none did. These are the commands Athena runs on the result.

rejected.option: Run only the crates the diff touches
rejected.why: An exhaustive match or struct literal in an untouched crate (athena-context, refusal_corpus, other CLI tests) could fail to compile unseen.

risks.risk: On a moved base the change-list comparison (path, status, mode, bytes) has no content hash, so two different edits of equal size to the same files would count as 'unchanged' (false disagreement).
risks.mitigation: The exact fingerprint is used whenever both base fingerprints are equal. The change list is used only when the base moved or a base fingerprint is missing, and it must be non-empty. The doc and the status label state the rule. Tests (c), (d), (e) cover it. The size of the error is a user-visible open question in the docs, not hidden.

risks.risk: A retry that landed after other jobs changed the same files could match on a change list by coincidence of path and size.
risks.mitigation: Both tries must be linked by the explicit 'try again on <job>' text and the retry must be Landed; at most one disagreement per gate per ended job.

risks.risk: Record fixtures for the CLI tests (Candidate2, Verification, Outcome) fail `check_record_file` validation or land in `invalid_records`, so counts come out empty.
risks.mitigation: Build them with the same canonical_path/to_json route as review.rs, and assert `invalid_records` is empty in the status test. The unit fixture uses the same builders, so a bad record shows in the `gate_counts` tests first.

risks.risk: A model-chosen gate may contain ']' or a newline and break the prefix parse.
risks.mitigation: `gate_counts` omits names containing ']' or newlines, `apply_answer` only accepts names from that list, and `gate_of_prevention` is anchored at the start and used only for Relax and Remove.

risks.risk: Adding a required `gate` property to the strict output schema could make a real model reject or omit it.
risks.mitigation: The property is nullable and `Answer.gate` has `#[serde(default)]`. Other kinds ignore it. The system prompt says to set it null otherwise.

risks.risk: Excluding Relax and Remove from `cause_key` changes the backfill for existing repositories.
risks.mitigation: No existing record has these kinds, so no existing group changes. The `gate_review_*` backfill tests and the existing hestia tests cover it.

risks.risk: Hestia queues loosening requests from thin evidence.
risks.mitigation: The request is a normal-priority review that cites the counts and asks for a justified change, not a removal. This job relaxes nothing, and the gate must exist in the counts.

risks.risk: A new enum variant or struct field breaks compilation or a lint in a crate the diff does not edit.
risks.mitigation: Step 10 runs the full-workspace fmt, clippy and test commands. `Answer.gate` is `#[serde(default)]` and `IntrospectionRecord` gains no field.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in `gate_counts.rs`. A fixture builds AnyRecords (Request, Candidate2, Verification, Outcome) in a tempdir and loads them with `store::Records::load_dir`. Cases: (a) `test` ends 5 rejected jobs, each with a landed 'try again on <job>' retry on the same base_fingerprint and the same candidate fingerprint, giving ends 5 / disagreements 5. (b) `fmt` ends 5 jobs: 3 retries landed with a different fingerprint on the same base, 2 retries were rejected again, giving disagreements 0. (c) Moved base: a retry landed with a different base_fingerprint and a different tree fingerprint but an identical change list counts as a disagreement. (d) Moved base with a different change list does not count. (e) Same base with different fingerprint but identical change list does not count. (f) A rejected job with no failed check counts under `verifier`. (g) A pre-existing-note failed check is not counted. (h) An admission rule is counted. (i) Order is most overruled first.
demonstrations.observes: `gate_counts(&records)` returns `test` with ends 5 and disagreements 5, and `fmt` with ends 5 and disagreements 0. Case (c) gives 1 and cases (d) and (e) give 0. The other cases hold as listed.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the counter missing, `test` would not give 5/5. Counting every landed retry regardless of change would give `fmt` 5. Comparing whole-tree fingerprints only would give 0 for case (c).
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `gate_counts::gate_counts(&Records)` (pure; guards: only request jobs with a Closed(Rejected) outcome and a verification, or Rejected/Failed with violations; retry link only via `reading::retried_job`; retry must be Closed(Landed)). Fixture: a `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod fixtures` that builds the AnyRecords and loads them through `Records::load_dir`, which exists (store.rs:353). The fixture module is added in step 1. demonstrations.method: An integration test in `introspection.rs` commits the job-chain fixture to the repo: `test` ended 5 jobs and was overruled 5 times, `fmt` ended 2 and was overruled 0. It runs the built binary `athena status` and `status --json` with `athena_bin(&fx)` (CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena). A display unit test renders a `StatusView` section with `gate_counts_lines`.
demonstrations.observes: Text output has a `gates` section with `test` 'ended 5 · overruled 5' listed before `fmt` 'ended 2 · overruled 0'. JSON has `gate_counts[0] == {gate: test, ends: 5, disagreements: 5}`. A repo with no gate ends prints no section and has no `gate_counts` key. `cargo test -p athena-cli gate` runs the display unit test `display::tests::gate_counts_lines_*`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the status field and display section, the output has no 'overruled' line and the JSON has no `gate_counts`.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: the `athena status` command, which reaches `Athena::status`, `StatusView` and display's status renderer. Fixture: committed AnyRecords in a real git repo (`Fixture`, which exists in tests/common). `athena_bin` exists at introspection.rs:291. The `gate_counts` field and `gate_counts_lines` are added in steps 4 and 5.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in the `introspect.rs` test module read the private `answer_schema()`, `SYSTEM_PROMPT` and `user_prompt(..)` directly. A CLI test also reads the prompt the scripted `Model` received (`model.prompts`).
demonstrations.observes: The `prevention_kind` enum equals [default, code-check, design-change, relax, remove]. `gate` is a required nullable property. `SYSTEM_PROMPT` contains 'can be wrong' and names relax and remove. The prompt JSON has a `gate_counts` array with `gate`, `ends` and `disagreements` for the fixture gates. `cargo test -p athena-cli --test introspection prompt_carries_gate_counts` checks the same on the prompt the Model received.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the edits, the enum has three values and the prompt has no `gate_counts` key.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `answer_schema()`, `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `user_prompt()` (introspect.rs:1006-1079), called in-module by tests. `user_prompt` gains a `gates` parameter in step 3. The CLI prompt capture already exists (the `Model.prompts` vector).

demonstrations.method: Run the three required checks, each as its own command, on the final tree. They cover every workspace crate, including those that construct or match the changed types (athena-data records, athena-context briefs, refusal_corpus, the CLI tests) and `system_facts_budgets_match_computed`, which is unaffected because no always-loaded prompt set changes.
demonstrations.observes: Clippy exits 0 with no warnings. `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo test --locked` also exit 0, and `cargo test --locked` reports no failed test in any crate, including all new `gate_counts::`, `gate_review*`, `records::` and CLI `introspection`/`review` tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missing `Relax`/`Remove` arm in `mistake_report` (status.rs ~1707), an `Answer` literal near introspect.rs:1848 lacking `gate`, an unregistered `gate_counts` module, or any lint or format drift would fail clippy, test (compile error) or fmt.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: the three Athena check commands themselves, run over the whole workspace with no fixture, fake or injection; the code under check is the real diff. They exist today. Step 10 runs them after `cargo fmt --all`.

demonstrations.method: Read the CHANGELOG.md diff and check each added line against the code diff.
demonstrations.observes: The new lines under [Unreleased] describe only: the gate counters (`gate_counts`, with the base-independent 'same change' rule), relax and remove prevention kinds with the `gate` answer field, Hestia's gate request, `cause_key` excluding relax/remove, the status section, and the defaults-loop.md update. They do not claim any gate was relaxed.

demonstrations.method: The status test of criterion 4 asserts the order (most overruled first, even though `fmt` sorts first by name and by an ends-only key would tie or reverse); then the diff is checked for governance files.
demonstrations.observes: `athena status` lists the most overruled gate first. `git diff --stat` lists none of athena.toml, defaults.toml or .github/workflows.
demonstrations.fails_without: An unsorted list, a sort by name, or a sort by ends would fail the order assertion in the chosen fixture.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 4: `athena status` through `Athena::status`, committed AnyRecords in the `Fixture` repo; the order assertion is in the same test.

open_questions: User: Should a later green rerun or the verifier passing the same change also count as a gate disagreement? The plan counts only the unchanged-landing signal, which is what criterion 1 requires. Adding the others later needs no record change.

User: Should the queued gate request name `athena.toml` in its Files line? The plan lists only `crates/` and `docs/`, because this job must not change governance files and the request is for Hestia's reviewer to decide.
